title: Reduce complete order-17 replay time by 8.17% (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

The new source-bound runner reduces the complete PR6208 four-command scientific replay median from 198.08 ms to 181.89 ms, 8.17% on the measured machine. Claim type: scoped exact-arithmetic implementation proof with a local performance result. No new kappa or Clifford theorem.

```text
five authenticated source inputs
  unchanged primary checker
    packed signed-integer Gaussian matrix products
    unchanged matrix / polynomial / Pauli / Bell / rejection predicates
  unchanged independent checker
```

The original source files retain their bytes. The only replaced primary function is matrix multiplication. Standard Kronecker substitution is credited as standard; this contribution supplies its bounded signed implementation, source binding and measured complete consumer. The implementation, proof and experiments were produced by Nick Petalas. apoursh / Armin Pourshafeie retains PR6208's construction and checkers; Nick Petalas retains PR6192's cap and Bell method; Ross Richardson retains the earlier cubic and Pauli-character lineage.

## Evidence

Five alternating complete bundles per side, including process startup, imports, authentication and output capture, execute 40 commands with zero failures and identical full stdout hashes. Baseline range 192.84–215.58 ms; packed range 176.45–201.92 ms. All five matched pairs favor the packed runner. Shared-machine noise makes the ranges overlap. An earlier five-pair run of the same kernel also improved the median by 6.80%, with disjoint ranges. A separate profile identifies exact multiplication as about half the original primary cost; Pauli construction/canonicalization, the independent checker and process startup limit the complete-path gain.

The new coverage guard compares every one of the 85 literal matrix products and all 21760 Gaussian output entries, then compares complete primary stdout, checks the actual packed CLI, and executes the unchanged independent checker. Arithmetic controls cover 16275 signed vector pairs, 71 matrix cases, 11 invalid inputs, five source mutations and the negative lower-tail borrow case.

Local CPython 3.12.15 checks pass:

- Both registered development-mode, warning-as-error commands, normal and optimized, in 0.2951 s and 0.3012 s.
- Registered metadata/replay, committed bytes, executable modes and declared source history.
- Official committed export/check and normal/optimized replay from a read-only export with empty PATH. All 14 payload files plus export receipt retain their bytes and modes.
- AST compilation and a maximum-function-length check. Ruff, mypy and pyflakes were unavailable; no separate lint pass is claimed.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
PY=~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12
"$PY" -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/packed-order17-replay
"$PY" -I -B -W error research/packed-order17-replay/verify.py
"$PY" -I -O -B -W error research/packed-order17-replay/verify.py
"$PY" -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/packed-order17-replay --check-source-history --check-modes
"$PY" -B research/packed-order17-replay/benchmark.py --output /absolute/external/path/benchmark.json
```

## Limitations

The timing comparison covers the same four original scientific commands, replacing only the two primary entry points. The new equivalence/regression guard adds verification work and is excluded from that comparison; no speedup of the generic package command is claimed. The gain is small in absolute time and is not a cross-platform performance guarantee.

The kernel is bounded to dimensions 1 through 16 and input integer components/denominators of at most 4096 bits. SHA checks precede compilation of the primary's authenticated source bytes, bypassing .pyc files. Documents and the unchanged independent CLI assume a stable checkout. Python allocation and the bounded dynamic module/function seam are documented in PROOF.md.

No selected scientific cold replay, physical/native supplier replay, formal-kernel proof or complete rounded multiplier was run. The five framework assumptions remain. This implementation improvement does not scientifically accept the predecessor or change the selected frontier.

## Open next questions

Does this bounded kernel improve another actual Gaussian-rational checker with larger numerator components? First profile its complete consumer and measure packing width. There is no evidence here for another caller; stop if the complete gain falls within noise.

## Related open work

- #6204 improves complete offline export-check performance through a different implementation. It does not change Gaussian arithmetic or this order-17 consumer.
- #6260 improves complete prefix-completion runtime using cached Hamming envelopes. It is separate verifier-engineering work on another consumer and changes no order-17 matrix product.
- #6265 changes encoded Machin termination and division costs in physical twiddle setup. That arithmetic consumer and resource claim are distinct from this exact matrix replay.

The completion refresh inspected this account's open PRs created since the advance CLAIM. No other new open PR studies the same order-17 consumer or its Gaussian matrix-product implementation. No same-instance numerical disagreement was identified, and no additional computations checked another contribution.

## CI notes

Both hosted checks, `plan` and `replay (research/packed-order17-replay)`, passed at head `c84082c700a5e391fe9bbbd62c1abef3004b129a` in [run 41049374676](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41049374676). The completed checks were read once; the successful run's exact head and conclusion were confirmed. All listed local checks also passed. Each registered command has a 120-second timeout and takes under one second locally.

Hosted CI certifies the registered finite checks and source bindings. It does not independently certify the local timing percentage, the written proof, supplier admission or a complete multiplication theorem.

## Merge danger

Two-way change, confined to the new opt-in research package. No shared code, frozen package, selected record or original credit line changes.
